Pilot Sample Size for Minimum Risk Point Estimation of the Coefficient of Variation

Source: R/seq_mr_cv.R
seq_mr_cv_pilot.Rd

Returns the pilot (first stage) sample size for the purely sequential minimum risk point estimation (MRPE) procedure for the population coefficient of variation \(\kappa = \sigma / \mu\) of Chattopadhyay and Kelley (2016). It needs only the two cost constants, so it can be computed before any data are collected.

Usage

seq_mr_cv_pilot(A, c, m_0 = 4, gamma = 0.49)

Arguments

A

The loss constant: the price of one unit of squared estimation error, in the same currency as c. The article builds it as the amount one is willing to pay to estimate the coefficient of variation to within \(\epsilon\), divided by \(\epsilon^2\) (for example \(1000 / 0.05^2 = 400000\)). A single positive number.

c

The cost of sampling one observation. A single positive number.

m_0

The smallest pilot size allowed: a whole number of at least 4 (the default), because the variance estimator uses the fourth central moment, which needs four observations.

gamma

The tuning constant of the stopping rule's correction term, strictly between 0 and 1/2. The default, 0.49, is the value Chattopadhyay and Kelley (2016) suggest. Use the same value in seq_mr_cv.

Value

A length one integer, the pilot sample size.

Details

The pilot size is Equation 24 of Chattopadhyay and Kelley (2016), $$m = \max\left\{m_0,\ \left\lceil (A/c)^{1/(2 + 2\gamma)} \right\rceil\right\},$$ where \(\lceil\cdot\rceil\) rounds up to the next whole number. The stopping rule of seq_mr_cv can never be met below \((A/c)^{1/(2 + 2\gamma)}\) observations, whatever the data, which is why the pilot starts there. In the article's worked example (\(A\) = 400,000, \(c\) = 75, \(\gamma\) = 0.49; p. 637) the pilot size is 18.

References

Chattopadhyay, B., & Kelley, K. (2016). Estimation of the coefficient of variation with minimum risk: A sequential method for minimizing sampling error and study cost. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 51(5), 627–648. doi:10.1080/00273171.2016.1203279

See also

seq_mr_cv for the stopping rule and seq_mr_cv_sensitivity to study the procedure before collecting data; the accuracy in parameter estimation companion seq_aipe_cv; in DMAR, mr_cv.

Other seq_mr_cv: seq_mr_cv(), seq_mr_sensitivity

Author

Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in, Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# The worked example of Chattopadhyay and Kelley (2016, p. 637): a home
# visit costs 75 dollars, and the team would pay 1,000 dollars to
# estimate the coefficient of variation to within 0.05.
seq_mr_cv_pilot(A = 1000 / 0.05^2, c = 75)
#> [1] 18
